facts.statement: Camposipterus lived during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 112 million years ago.
facts.quote: Fossil remains of Camposipterus dated back to the Early Cretaceous, about 112 million years ago.

facts.statement: Camposipterus was a pterodactyloid pterosaur found in England.
facts.quote: Camposipterus is a genus of pterodactyloid pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous of England.

facts.statement: Harry Govier Seeley originally named the species Ptenodactylus nasutus in 1869 based on fossils from Haslingfield, Cambridgeshire.
facts.quote: In 1869, Harry Govier Seeley, based on a fossil found at Haslingfield, Cambridgeshire, named Ptenodactylus nasutus

facts.statement: Taissa Rodrigues and Alexander Kellner established the genus Camposipterus in 2013 after determining the species was distinct from Anhanguera fittoni.
facts.quote: In 2013, Taissa Rodrigues and Alexander Wilhelm Armin Kellner concluded firstly that Pterodactylus fittoni was not a part of the genus Anhanguera and secondly that Ornithocheirus nasutus was not identical to it regardless.

facts.statement: The genus name Camposipterus honors Brazilian paleontologist Diogenes de Almeida Campos and the Greek word for wing.
facts.quote: The generic name combines that of the Brazilian paleontologist Diogenes de Almeida Campos with a Latinized Greek πτερόν, pteron, "wing".

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found in the Cambridge Greensand, which dates to the Cenomanian but likely contains older Albian fossils.
facts.quote: The holotype, CAMSM B 54556, had been found in a layer of the Cambridge Greensand dating from the Cenomanian but probably containing reworked fossils from the older Albian.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil consists only of the front part of a snout.
facts.quote: It consists of the front part of a snout.

facts.statement: In side view, the snout of Camposipterus is rounded.
facts.quote: In side view the snout is rounded.

facts.statement: The snout of Camposipterus bears no crest.
facts.quote: The snout bears no crest.

facts.statement: The palate of Camposipterus curves upwards.
facts.quote: The palate curves upwards.

facts.statement: The first pair of teeth is located at the tip of the snout.
facts.quote: The first tooth pair is located in the snout tip.

facts.statement: The snout tip is flat and wider than it is tall when viewed from the front.
facts.quote: The snout tip is flat, in front view wider than tall.

facts.statement: The second and third pairs of teeth are obliquely pointed sideways.
facts.quote: the second and third tooth pairs are obliquely pointed sideways

facts.statement: Rodrigues and Kellner assigned Camposipterus to the clade Anhangueria but placed it incertae sedis due to an unknown position.
facts.quote: Rodrigues and Kellner assigned Camposipterus to the clade Anhangueria, but incertae sedis, thus in an unknown position.

facts.statement: A 2019 study by Jacobs et al. placed Camposipterus within the family Ornithocheiridae as the sister taxon of Cimoliopterus.
facts.quote: In 2019, Jacobs et al. published a phylogenetic analysis that placed Camposipterus within the family Ornithocheiridae, more specifically the sister taxon of Cimoliopterus.

facts.statement: Researchers express uncertainty regarding the validity of assigning certain species to the genus Camposipterus.
facts.quote: The question marks indicate the uncertainty of the authors about the correctness of the move.

facts.statement: In 2025, Pêgas assigned O. colorhinus to the genus Cimoliopterus based on its close relationship to C. cuvieri.
facts.quote: In 2025, Pêgas also assigned "O." colorhinus to the genus Cimoliopterus due to finding it closely related to C. cuvieri.

facts.statement: Camposipterus(?) sedgwickii was reassigned to the genus Aerodraco in 2020.
facts.quote: This species was reassigned to the genus Aerodraco in 2020.

facts.statement: The genus name Camposipterus combines the surname of Brazilian paleontologist Diogenes de Almeida Campos with the Greek word for 'wing'.
facts.quote: El nombre del género combina el paellido del paleontólogo brasileño Diogenes de Almeida Campos con el griego latinizadok πτερόν, pteron, que significa "ala".

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found in the Cambridge Greensand formation, dating to the Cenomanian but likely containing reworked fossils from the older Albian.
facts.quote: El holotipo CAMSM B 54556 fue encontrado en una capa de la Cambridge Greensand que data del Cenomaniense pero es probable que contenga fósiles reelaborados del más antiguo Albiense.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of the front part of the snout.
facts.quote: Consiste en la parte frontal del hocico.

facts.statement: In 2013, Rodrigues and Kellner transferred two additional species into the genus Camposipterus.
facts.quote: Rodrigues & Kellner en 2013 trasladaron dos especies más a este género.

facts.statement: The question mark in the species names indicates that the authors were not certain about the validity of transferring those species to the genus.
facts.quote: El signo de interrogación indica que los autores aún no están seguros de lo correcto de este traslado.

facts.statement: Richard Owen named Pterodactylus sedgwickii in 1859 based on the front part of a snout from the Cambridge Greensand.
facts.quote: Pterodactylus sedgwickii fue nombrado en 1859 por Richard Owen basándose en el espécimen CAMSM B54422, la parte frontal de un hocico del Cambridge Greensand.

facts.statement: In 1859, Owen also referred a front part of lower jaws, specimen CAMSM B54421, though this piece is not from the same individual as the holotype.
facts.quote: Owen en 1859 también refirió una parte frontal de unas mandíbulas inferiores, el espécimen CAMSM B54421.

facts.statement: Seeley named Ptenodactylus colorhinus in 1869 and Ornithocheirus colorhinus in 1870 based on two front snout parts from the Cambridge Greensand.
facts.quote: En 1869, Seeley también nombró a Ptenodactylus colorhinus, denominándolo en 1870 Ornithocheirus colorhinus basado en los sintipos CAMSM B54431 y CAMSM B54432, ambos partes frontales del hocico de Cambridge Greensand.

facts.statement: The species name colorhinus means 'joined nose' derived from Greek words for 'joined' and 'nose'.
facts.quote: Su nombre de la especie significa "nariz acoplada" from the Greek κόλος, kolos, "acoplado", y ῥίς, rhis, "nariz".

facts.statement: In 2001, David Unwin considered this species a subjective synonym of Anhanguera cuvieri, a view not accepted by later researchers.
facts.quote: En 2001, Unwin consideró a esta especie como un sinónimo más moderno de Anhanguera cuvieri.

facts.statement: Rodrigues and Kellner treated Camposipterus as a clade defined by a unique combination of traits rather than a single shared derived character.
facts.quote: Rodrigues & Kellner trataron a Camposipterus como un grupo o clado. No se pudieron establecer sinapomorfias, siendo en cambio establecida una combinación única de rasgos, sin estar presente ningún rasgo singular.

facts.statement: The snout is rounded in side view, lacks a crest, has an expanded front, and the palate curves upward.
facts.quote: En vista lateral el hocico es redondeado. E hocico carece de cresta. La parte frontal del hocico está expandida. El paladar se curva hacia arriba.

facts.statement: Camposipterus nasutus has a unique dental density of three teeth per three centimeters at the front of the jaw and 2.5 teeth at the rear.
facts.quote: Rodrigues y Kellner establecieron dos autapomorfias de Camposipterus nasutus. En la parte frontal del bode de la mandíbula hay una densidad de tres dientes por tres centímetros, en la parte posterior esta densidad es de 2.5dientes.

facts.statement: The snout tip is flat and wider than it is high when viewed from the front.
facts.quote: La punta del hocico es plana, en vista frontal es más ancha que alta.

facts.statement: The unique combination of traits for C. nasutus includes a straight or slightly curved upper snout profile, a palate midline extending to the back of the second tooth pair, gradually increasing tooth spacing posteriorly, obliquely pointing second and third tooth pairs, and a slightly expanded snout front.
facts.quote: La combinación única de rasgos es: el perfil superior del hocico es derecho o levemente curvado; la línea media del paladar se extiende hacia adelante hasta el nivel del margen posterior del segundo par de dientes; hacia la región posterior la distancia entre los dientes se incrementa gradualmente; el segundo y tercer pares de dientes apuntan hacia los lados en forma oblicua; el frente del hocico se expande levemente.

facts.statement: Seeley speculated that a depression on the snout might serve for lip attachment, but pterosaurs instead had horny coverings.
facts.quote: Seeley especuló que esta área podría servir de sujeción a un labio, pero los pterosaurios tenían en cambio cubiertas córneas.

facts.statement: Rodrigues and Kellner assigned Camposipterus to the clade Anhangueria but placed it as an incertae sedis, meaning its exact position is uncertain.
facts.quote: Rodrigues y Kellner asignaron a Camposipterus a un nuevo clado denominado Anhangueria, pero como un incertae sedis, es decir, en una posición incierta.

facts.statement: Some cladistic analyses suggested Camposipterus was more derived than Cimoliopterus but less derived than Cearadactylus atrox.
facts.quote: Algunos análisis cladísticos publicadps en el artículo de descripción sugirieron una posición en el árbol evolutivo más derivada que la de Cimoliopterus pero por debajo de la de Cearadactylus atrox.

facts.statement: Camposipterus lived during the Albian stage, from 106.3 to 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (106.3 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Camposipterus belongs to the parent group Anhangueria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Anhangueria

facts.statement: Camposipterus is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: There are three recorded fossil occurrences of Camposipterus in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 3
